how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py --api https://brotato.wiki.spellsandguns.com/api.php --titles <pages> (page text as rendered by the wiki, link markup removed; the wiki's own search answers nothing, so page titles came from its list of all pages). Every quoted fragment below was checked, by script, to appear word for word (spaces collapsed) in the page text read at the revision named. Table rows on the Enemies page are quoted as the reader prints them: columns separated by '||', in the order Health, +hp/wave, Speed, Damage, +dmg/wave, Knockback Resistance, Materials Dropped, Consumable Drop Rate, Loot Crate Drop Rate, First Wave Appearing, ID. A 'D1 : 4' first wave means the enemy only starts on Danger 1 and up, at wave 4.

lines.line: Summary: An enemy that runs away from you instead of fighting. Catch and kill it and it drops a Loot Crate plus 8 materials.

quoted: Runs away from the character, drops a Loot Crate and 8 Materials on death

lines.line: Tips: It can only appear from wave 3. Each time it gets a chance to appear, the odds are 10%: the first chance comes 25 seconds after a wave begins, and another every 15 seconds after that.

quoted: Has 10% chance to spawn 25 seconds into a wave, and every 15 seconds thereafter.

lines.line: Summary: An enemy that hunts down materials, eats them, and grows as it eats.

quoted: Seeks materials to eat them; eating materials makes it grow.

lines.line: Weak points: Its first version is fast but fragile.

quoted: Fast but fragile.

lines.line: Tips: Killing it drops the materials it ate: all of them from its first version, twice as many from the second and three times as many from the third. The later versions are slower but have more health. It has only a 3% chance to appear, and the chance is rolled 10 seconds after a wave begins.

quoted: Killing it makes it drop all the materials it ate.
Loses speed but gains max HP.
Killing it makes it drop twice the amount of materials it ate.
Loses more speed but gains even more max HP.
Killing it makes it drop triple the materials eaten.
Has 3% chance to spawn 10 seconds into a wave.

lines.line: Summary: A Slasher Egg sits still; leave it alone for 5 seconds and a Slasher hatches from it. A Slasher follows you but backs off when you get close, and hits with a vertical slash from medium range.

quoted: Stays still, dies and spawns a Slasher after 5 seconds unless killed
Follows the character, runs away if too close, slashes vertically dealing damage from medium range

lines.line: Weak points: An egg only hatches if it is still alive when its 5 seconds run out, so killing it first means no Slasher.

quoted: Stays still, dies and spawns a Slasher after 5 seconds unless killed

lines.line: Tips: Neither is met on Danger 0: both start on Danger 1, Slashers from wave 4 and eggs from wave 7. A Slasher starts with 50 health and gains 25 each wave, while an egg starts with 5 and gains 3.

quoted: As Danger 1 adds more enemies, they only start spawning for Danger 1 and up.

lines.line: Summary: A chaser that hurts you on touch and gets faster with every second it keeps chasing you.

quoted: Chases the character, damages on touch, keeps getting faster each second

lines.line: Tips: It first appears at wave 11, where the page works its health out as 250 (10 to start plus 24 for each wave after the first), and that is 40% higher on Danger 5. Its speed climbs from 150 to 600 while the page gives your own base speed as 450, and its speed does not change with the wave or the Danger level.

quoted: Pursuers don't show up before wave 11, but at wave 11 they would have 10 HP + 10x24 HP = 250 HP. (It is 40% higher for Danger 5 in both cases.)
As a reference for speed, your own base speed is 450.
Damage works the same way, while their Speed doesn't change with Wave or Danger level.

lines.line: Summary: An enemy that moves around you. When your ranged weapons hit it, it answers half the time by shooting out projectiles in random directions.

quoted: Moves around player.
When hit by Ranged Weapons, 50% chance to fire projectiles in random directions.

lines.line: Tips: The 50% chance applies to ranged hits only, because hits from melee weapons do not make it fire. It starts with 15 health and gains 4 each wave, moves at a random speed between 325 and 375, and is only met from Danger 1 up, starting at wave 4.

quoted: (Melee Weapon hits don't spawn projectiles.)
Some enemies spawn with a random movement speed. For example, a Baby Alien can spawn with a movement speed between 200 and 300, or a Fly between 325 and 375.
As Danger 1 adds more enemies, they only start spawning for Danger 1 and up.

lines.line: Summary: An Elite enemy (Danger 2 and up) that opens by putting 15 Slasher Eggs on the field, then shoots at you, and later runs away while spawning Tentacles.

quoted: Spawns 15 Slasher Eggs
Shoots 5 projectiles each second to the player
Last 10 seconds, runs away from the player, spawning Tentacles
=== Elites (Danger 2+)

lines.line: Tips: Its eggs hatch into Slashers after 5 seconds unless they are killed first. From 10 seconds in it fires 5 shots a second at you, and from the 30-second mark it spends 10 seconds running away and spawning Tentacles before going back to shooting. A Tentacle follows you, backs off if you get close, and attacks in a V shape at medium range. Killing the Monk drops a Legendary Loot Crate holding a guaranteed Legendary (tier 4) item.

quoted: Stays still, dies and spawns a Slasher after 5 seconds unless killed
Mutation 2(30 sec): Last 10 seconds, runs away from the player, spawning Tentacles Returns to Mutation 1
Follows the character, runs away if too close, attacks in "V" shape from medium range
Elites spawn at Elite Waves and drop legendary Loot Crates on death containing a guaranteed tier 4 item (Legendary).

lines.line: Summary: An Elite enemy (Danger 2 and up) that attacks by throwing out circles and bursts of projectiles, in three stages.

quoted: Random walk pattern - spawns a big circle of projectiles around itself every 0.3 seconds
Chases the player - spawning 12 projectiles around itself in random pattern every 0.4 seconds
Chases the player - spawns a 3 of projectiles in random directions every 0.01 - 0.15 seconds
=== Elites (Danger 2+)

lines.line: Tips: At first it wanders at random, putting out a big circle of projectiles around itself every 0.3 seconds. From 60% health or 30 seconds in, it chases you and fires 12 projectiles around itself at random, every 0.4 seconds. From 30% health or 45 seconds in, it chases you and shoots projectiles off in random directions, once every 0.01 to 0.15 seconds. Killing it drops a Legendary Loot Crate holding a guaranteed Legendary (tier 4) item.

quoted: Mutation 1(60%HP/30 sec): Chases the player - spawning 12 projectiles around itself in random pattern every 0.4 seconds
Mutation 2(30%HP/45 sec): Chases the player - spawns a 3 of projectiles in random directions every 0.01 - 0.15 seconds
Elites spawn at Elite Waves and drop legendary Loot Crates on death containing a guaranteed tier 4 item (Legendary).

lines.line: Summary: A cheap Tier 2 damage item with a catch: it sends Lampreys after you at the beginning of the next wave.

quoted: Bait provides a significant amount of Damage at a cheap cost, but it comes with a risk.
between 7 and 8 Lamprey enemies will spawn at the start of the wave to chase you down.

lines.line: Uses: It gives +8% damage and costs 25. Killing the Lampreys it brings pays 7 to 8 extra materials.

quoted: +8 % Damage
Price 25
if you manage to kill them, you'll earn yourself an additional 7-8 Materials

lines.line: Tips: Between 7 and 8 Lampreys come at you, and the page calls them quite dangerous. A Lamprey charges at you every 1.5 seconds and fires projectiles out to either side as it goes.

quoted: The Lampreys are quite dangerous enemies that will charge you while firing projectiles.
Follows the player, charges to the player every 1.5 seconds, shooting projectiles to its left and right during the charge

lines.line: Summary: A Tier 2 economy item that gives the materials you pick up a chance to count double.

quoted: +5% chance to double the value of picked up materials

lines.line: Uses: Each one adds 5% to the chance that a picked-up material is worth double, both as money and as experience. It also gives +6 Luck and +2 Engineering and takes away 5% damage. It costs 40, and you can hold up to 20.

quoted: Metal detector gives an additive 5% per item chance for any Materials you pick up to have double the value. You gain both double the Money and double Experience.
+6 Luck +2 Engineering -5 % Damage
Price 40 Limit 20

lines.line: Tips: Bagged materials paid out at the start of a wave are worth 4 times as much when it triggers, so you end up with about the same on average whether you let them get bagged or not. The same 4 times applies to Buccaneer's double materials. The page calls it very powerful for Endless Mode.

quoted: Double value materials from bagged materials dropped at the beginning of a wave gives 4x the value when metal detector triggers.
This means you gain same amount of materials on average if you let your materials get bagged or not.
Buccaneer's double materials ability gives 4x materials when Metal Detector triggers.
It is a very powerful item for Endless Mode, where the ability to gain additional materials is highly valued.

lines.line: Summary: A Tier 2 economy item that raises how much you get back when you recycle weapons and items.

quoted: Gain 35% more materials from recycling items

lines.line: Uses: Without it, recycling returns 25% of an item's price. The machine adds 35%, so you get 60% back. It costs 35, and you can only hold one.

quoted: The Default is to get 25% back when recycling. Recycling Machine can increase this value by 35% for a total of 60% back.
Price 35 Limit 1
Only 1 of each unique item can be equipped

lines.line: Tips: Entrepreneur's +25% stacks with it for 85% back. The payout follows an item's current price, so it grows with inflation and shrinks if you hold Coupons.

quoted: This stacks with the +25% from Entrepreneur for a total of 85%.
Rewards for recycling are based upon the current price of the item, so it increases with inflation, but decreases if you have coupons

lines.line: Summary: A Tier 2 economy item that adds 20% to the materials you carry out of the shop at the start of every wave.

quoted: +20% of your materials at the start of waves (stops working at wave 20)
The Piggy Bank give you 20% of your Materials when you exit the shop and start a new wave.

lines.line: Uses: Leave the shop holding 100 materials and the wave starts with 120. The bonus is money only, with no experience. It costs 40 and you can hold one. In Endless Mode it stops working after wave 20.

quoted: For example, if you leave the shop with 100 materials, you will start the wave with 120.
Piggy Bank doesn't give Experience. It only gives you the Currency Part of Materials.
Price 40 Limit 1
While playing in Endless Mode, Piggy Bank stops functioning after wave 20.

lines.line: Tips: The gain compounds: any materials you hold back more than double within four waves and grow about 6.2 times over ten. It is best bought early and saved up, and the page suggests skipping it if you cannot save between rounds. It suits Demon and Streamer, and Saver begins with it.

quoted: Any amount held back will more than double over four waves, and will have multiplied by ~6.2 over ten waves.
Like other Economic items, it is more powerful when bought early, and of little value when bought in the late game.
If you can't save up materials between rounds, it might be better to skip the Piggy Bank
The Piggy Bank has strong synergy with characters such as Demon or Streamer
The Character Saver starts the game with Piggy Bank

lines.line: Summary: A Tier 1 item that gives your hits a chance to set enemies on fire.

quoted: Scared Sausage gives any weapon hit, any projectile hit, and any hit by an Engineering structure a 25% chance to inflict burn.

lines.line: Uses: Each one gives hits a 25% chance to burn, so holding 4 reaches 100%. The burn deals 1 + (100%) damage every second, lasting at most 3 seconds, as the page writes it. It costs 25 and the limit is 4.

quoted: Each additional Scared Sausage increases the chance to inflict burn by another 25%. It is possible to reach a 100% chance by holding 4 Scared Sausages (which is the count limit for this item).
The burn effect from Scared Sausage does 1 + (100%) damage each second, for up to 3 seconds.
Price 25 Limit 4

lines.line: Tips: It also adds 1 to the damage of any other burn, such as the Flamethrower or Incendiary Turret, but a point of Elemental Damage is cheaper than the item, so it is not worth buying just for that. Engineering structures can burn enemies, and so can explosions from Bull, Landmines and Rocket Launcher. Baby Elephant, Cyberball and Riposte cannot, and neither can explosions from Spicy Sauce or Rip and Tear.

quoted: Scared Sausage passively adds 1 to the burn damage of any burn (e.g Flamethrower or Incendiary Turret), except other Scared Sausages.
Since Scared Sausage costs more than 1 Elemental Damage, it is not economical to buy the item only to increase the burn damage of weapons.
All Engineering structures can inflict burn, via direct hit as well as explosion hit
The Explosion from Bull or Landmines can inflict burn, as do explosions from weapons such as Rocket Launcher.
Baby Elephant, Cyberball, or Riposte can not inflict burn.
The Explosion from items such as Spicy Sauce or Rip and Tear can not inflict burn.

lines.line: Summary: A Tier 3 damage item that raises your damage versus Elites and bosses.

quoted: Silver Bullet grants 25% Bonus damage against Elites and Bosses

lines.line: Uses: Each one raises your damage versus Elites and bosses by 25%. It costs 70.

quoted: Silver Bullet grants 25% Bonus damage against Elites and Bosses
Price 70
The Silver Bullet Item can help you kill the elites, as it increases the damage you deal to them by 25%

lines.line: Tips: Worked example: an attack that does 100 damage reaches 200 with 100% Damage, then 250 with one Silver Bullet, and 400 with four. Jack's +125% bonus versus bosses and Elites is the same effect, and the two add together.

quoted: if you have an attack that deals 100 damage, and you have 100% Damage, bringing the attack to 200.
bringing it to a total of 250 damage. If you had 4 Silver Bullets, the attack would deal 400 damage.
Silver Bullet is additive with Jack's +125% against Bosses and Elites. It is the same effect.

lines.line: Summary: A cheap Tier 1 economy item that makes the items in the shop cost less.

quoted: Coupon reduces the Items Price secondary stat by 5%.

lines.line: Uses: Each Coupon takes 5% off shop item prices, and you can hold up to 5 for 25% off. It costs 15.

quoted: Coupon reduces the Items Price secondary stat by 5%.
You can stack up to 5 Coupons for a maximum 25% price reduction.
Price 15 Limit 5

lines.line: Tips: No other item changes shop prices, and this one does not change what rerolls cost. With the character Entrepreneur and 5 Coupons the cut reaches 50%, the most possible. The page ranks it with the stronger items and says it is nearly always worth buying, unless it is first seen around waves 16 to 18 or after.

quoted: It is the only item in the game that modifies shop prices.
Coupon does not modify the cost of rerolls in the Shop or rerolling Upgrades.
The highest cost reduction possible is 50%, on the character Entrepreneur and having the maximum amount of 5 coupons.
It is generally considered one of the better items in the game, and is nearly always bought in shop when seen, unless it is found at wave 16-18 or later.

lines.line: Summary: A Tier 4 healing item that gives a large amount of health regeneration, and more of it as each wave goes on.

quoted: +10 HP Regeneration +2 HP Regeneration every 5 seconds until the end of the wave

lines.line: Uses: It gives +10 HP Regeneration, plus another +2 for every 5 seconds that pass in a wave until that wave ends, and takes away 10 Luck. It costs 95 and is unlocked by winning a run with Doctor.

quoted: The Medkit gives a base +10 HP Regeneration and an additional +2 HP regeneration per 5 seconds of time that has passed during a wave.
-10 Luck
Price 95 Unlocked by Win a run with Doctor

lines.line: Tips: The page's table shows the extra regeneration reaching +34 by the 85-second mark, which it calls very potent for the wave 20 boss fight, a fight that lasts 90 seconds.

quoted: +32 !! +34 This makes the Medkit very potent at healing during the 90 second Boss Fight on Wave 20.
